subject: Quasar Labs: node reservation overlap & thermal binning question for late-stage POC
messages:
From: Olivia Ramos <olivia@quasarlabs.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@quasarlabs.ai
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity request — late-stage POC (QSR-2029)

Hi Soojin,

We're ramping the Quasar POC into a week-long late-stage soak before enterprise exec review. We need to lock a short window of dedicated capacity to guarantee test determinism. High-level ask: 32x A100 80GB-equivalent (or capacity match) for a 90-day window starting 2029-06-10, sustained runs ~12 hours/day, peak concurrency 48 concurrent sessions. Region preference: us-west.

A couple of operational questions that matter for our tests:
- Thermal binning / sustained perf: we need to understand whether the nodes you'll allocate share thermal/clock bins that could cause step-down under long sustained loads.
- Overlap risk: we may need to extend for another 30 days if execs request more validation.

Please advise on provisional reservation steps, estimated lead-time for hard hold versus soft-reserve, and any documentation you need from procurement. Also include any MOU or activation window constraints.

Thanks,
Olivia Ramos
VP of ML Platforms
Quasar Labs
olivia@quasarlabs.ai

Attachment: quasar-requirements-v1.pdf (application spec, 120KB stub)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity request — late-stage POC (QSR-2029)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear rundown. We can support a provisional reservation while we confirm node-level characteristics. Quick answers up front:
- We can provision an equivalent of 32 x A100-80GB capacity in us-west, but final binning depends on the pool we allocate from.
- Soft-reserve (30-day provisional) is doable with a nominal commitment and a 14-day activation window. Hard hold requires legal/finance sign-off and typically a 60–90 day lead (depends on current commitments).

Looping in Karthik for an inventory and thermal/clock-bin read. Ben — I think this is a reasonable candidate for a short MOU + activation hold. Can you propose next steps?

— Soojin

Hi team,

Inventory snapshot (preliminary) attached — node-inventory-20290521.csv. TL;DR: across our us-west dedicated pools we can hit the equivalent of 32 A100-80GB-capacity nodes for the 2029-06-10 start date with the following caveats:
- Distribution: to reduce thermal bin variance we'll allocate across three racks in the same AZ (rack-level redundancy). That reduces risk of clock-down under sustained load but introduces slight cross-rack network variance (~2–6ms P95).
- Thermal binning: most nodes in the pool are bin B/C (sustained turbo at 1.55–1.6GHz under sustained loads). A small subset of newer chassis are bin A (1.65GHz sustained). If you need strict parity across all 32 nodes, we can cherry-pick from bin A/B but that will lengthen provisioning by ~7–10 days and costs ~8% premium.
- Spare capacity: we're currently holding a 10% buffer for committed Dedicated customers; a soft-reserve can be implemented by marking nodes as "provisional" in inventory and reducing the buffer to 5% for your deal, subject to contract terms.

Questions for Quasar: can you confirm the concurrency profile (48 peak sessions: are those short bursts or sustained long-running jobs?) and whether homogeneous binning across all nodes is a hard requirement for your validation? Also confirm whether you prefer a single pool allocation or multiple smaller pools to isolate thermal variance.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: node-inventory-20290521.csv (CSV stub, 34 rows)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity request — late-stage POC (QSR-2029)

Olivia — good to meet you (virtually). We can move quickly here. Proposed path:
1) Sign short MOU (attached draft) to put a 30-day soft-reserve in place. That holds the provisional nodes and sets an activation window.
2) Choose between: (A) homogeneous bin pick (A/B only) with 7–10 day lead and ~8% premium, or (B) mixed-bin allocation across three racks with slightly higher P95 variance but immediate availability.
3) If you need an extension beyond 90 days we can convert to a committed Dedicated block (pricing/discounts to be negotiated).

I attached a draft MOU (qsr-mou-draft.pdf) — it includes: provisional hold start, activation window, cancellation terms, and cursory SLA commitments for uptime and token throughput. If you sign that DocuSign link we can set the provisional flag in inventory the same business day.
